subject: walrus
title: A Walrus Can Suck 6,000 Clams Out of Their Shells in One Meal

scenes.text: A walrus eats thousands of clams and never chews a single shell.
It feels along the dark seafloor with 400 to 700 whiskers, sensitive enough to tell shells apart.
To dig clams out, it blasts powerful jets of water into the mud.
Then its tongue works like a piston, sucking the soft body straight out of the shell.
One feeding session can mean up to six thousand clams.
No cracking, no chewing. Just thousands of empty shells.

description:
A walrus can eat as many as 6,000 clams in a single feeding session, without cracking them.
It finds them with 400 to 700 sensitive whiskers, digs them out with jets of water, and its piston-like tongue sucks the soft parts out of the shell. In one measurement a walrus produced suction of about minus 119 kPa underwater.
What's the most you've ever eaten in one meal?
first_comment: Up to 6,000 clams in one sitting. Which animal do you think has the biggest appetite?
